assignmentHtml.task: Audit claims A1 and A2 about Hayabusa2. Starting point: https://www.isas.jaxa.jp/en/missions/spacecraft/current/hayabusa2.html. Key questions: (1) Exact date of capsule landing with Ryugu samples — was it 14 December 2020? Was the opening of the sample container the same event as the capsule landing or a separate later event? (2) Did returning the capsule end the spacecraft's flight? (3) Were organic compounds found in Ryugu material? Does that demonstrate living organisms once inhabited Ryugu? Find original JAXA publications, papers on organic analysis, and any contamination control details. Report exact findings with source URLs.
assignmentHtml.context: Mission: Hayabusa2. Target: asteroid Ryugu. Claims A1-A2 are to be audited: A1 says capsule landed 14 Dec 2020 and container opening was same event; A2 says returning capsule ended flight and organic compounds demonstrate living organisms once inhabited Ryugu. These are claims to check, not supplied facts. Some may be accurate, some mixed, some over-inferencing.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: Verdict on each component of A1 and A2, with corrected text, dates, units, source URLs. Specifically: capsule landing date, whether container opening was same or separate event, spacecraft status after capsule release, what organics were found and in what form, whether any claim of past life is supported.

answerHtml: A1 contains two factual errors. The Hayabusa2 sample capsule landed on 6 December 2020 (JST) / 5 December 2020 UTC at Woomera, Australia — not 14 December 2020. The 14 December date is when JAXA confirmed grains of Ryugu material were present inside the sample container, a separate event from the landing. The sample container opening was indeed a separate later event, not the same as the capsule landing. A2 is partially correct and partially incorrect. Returning the capsule did NOT end the spacecraft's flight; Hayabusa2 performed trajectory correction maneuvers after capsule separation on 5 December 2020 and continued its Extended Mission toward asteroid 1998 KY26 (arrival ~2031), successfully flying by Torifune in July 2026. Organic compounds WERE found in Ryugu material — including 15+ amino acids, aliphatic amines, carboxylic acids, PAHs, and N-heterocycles (Naraoka et al. 2023), plus all five canonical nucleobases (Koga et al. 2026). However, none of these findings demonstrate that living organisms once inhabited Ryugu. Every scientific paper explicitly attributes the organics to abiotic processes: amino acids are racemic (D/L ≈ 1), nucleobase distributions deviate from Chargaff's rule, and NASA states organics 'can also be made by chemical reactions that don't involve life.'

evidence.snippet: On December 6, 2020, JAXA recovered the body of the capsule, the heat shields, and the parachute of the Hayabusa2 re-entry capsule in the Woomera Prohibited Area (WPA). After the capsule separation, the spacecraft performed trajectory correction maneuvers three times every 30 minutes to depart from the Earth's sphere from 15:30 to 16:30 on December 5 (JST)... The current status of the spacecraft is normal.
evidence.supports: Capsule landing date was 6 December 2020 (JST); spacecraft remained operational after capsule separation.

evidence.snippet: The Hayabusa2 re-entry capsule was recovered in Woomera, Australia on December 6, 2020 and delivered to the JAXA Sagamihara Campus on December 8... On December 14, a sample of grains of black sand thought to be derived from asteroid Ryugu was confirmed to be inside the sample container.
evidence.supports: 14 December 2020 was the date of confirming Ryugu grains in the container, a separate event from the 6 December capsule landing.

evidence.snippet: On December 15 at 11:00 JST, chamber A in the sample container was opened and it was confirmed to contain the sample from asteroid Ryugu that is thought to have been collected and stored during the time of the first touchdown (February 22, 2019).
evidence.supports: Sample chamber A was opened on 15 December 2020, well after the 6 December capsule landing — confirming container opening was a separate, later event.

evidence.snippet: After returning to the Earth in December 2020, Hayabusa2 separated the sample capsule and left for a new journey into deep space. The Extended Mission will use the remaining ion engine fuel (Xenon), of which about half currently remains. The next target destination is asteroid 1998 KY26 and arrival is scheduled for 2031.
evidence.supports: Hayabusa2 did not end its mission with capsule return; it continued its Extended Mission with ~50% xenon remaining.

evidence.snippet: Fifteen amino acids, including glycine, alanine, and α-aminobutyric acid, were identified. These were present as racemic mixtures (equal right- and left-handed abundances), consistent with an abiotic origin... The wide variety of molecules identified indicates that prolonged chemical processes contributed to the synthesis of soluble organics on Ryugu or its parent body.
evidence.supports: Organic compounds (including amino acids) were found in Ryugu samples; racemic mixtures confirm abiotic (non-biological) origin, not past life.

evidence.snippet: However, organic molecules can also be made by chemical reactions that don't involve life, supporting the hypothesis that chemical reactions in asteroids can make some of life's ingredients.
evidence.supports: NASA explicitly states detected organics do not imply biological activity; they are prebiotic chemicals formed by non-biological reactions.

evidence.snippet: The observed nucleobase distributions in the Ryugu samples deviate from Chargaff's rule—which states that purine and pyrimidine bases occur in a 1:1 ratio in the DNA of all organisms—further supporting the interpretation that the nucleobases identified... are of non-biological, extraterrestrial origin.
evidence.supports: All five nucleobases detected but explicitly attributed to non-biological origin; no claim of past life made.

evidence.snippet: In the Hayabusa2 metal sealing system, the softer aluminum alloy part of the container lid was pressed onto the inner edge (harder Al alloy) of the sample container with a force of ~2700 N... The gas pressure inside the sample container demonstrates that the newly developed metal sealing system worked more efficiently than the Hayabusa sample container...
evidence.supports: Contamination control was rigorous: hermetic metal seal, 100-hour recovery race, ISO6 cleanroom, nitrogen-purged handling. This ensures organics detected are genuinely extraterrestrial, not terrestrial contamination.
